a.address_statement: The current artmuseum.pl pages list the main museum at Marszałkowska 103, 00-110 Warsaw. The Visit page gives the same address, plus an email and phone number.
a.notes: Moved: the museum opened its permanent building on Plac Defilad in October 2024 (search results: notesfrompoland.com and a city tourism listing give ul. Marszałkowska 103, 00-110 Warszawa). Older addresses seen and rejected as outdated: Wybrzeże Kościuszkowskie 22, 00-124 Warszawa (temporary exhibition space on the Vistula, listed by glossary.internationaleonline.org and on archived archiwum.artmuseum.pl pages); Pańska 3 (earlier headquarters; the Visit page still lists the Offices there, not a public venue); ul. Emilii Plater 51 (one older page). Cinema KINOMUZEUM and the reading room are at the same Marszałkowska address. Evidence text is from the WebSearch summary of artmuseum.pl results; the summary names the Visit page as the source of the address and refers to the other current artmuseum.pl pages (contact-1) generally.

b.address_statement: The museum sits at Marszałkowska 103, 00-110 Warsaw, in the Śródmieście district. Since 25 October 2024, MSN has been based at ul. Marszałkowska 103.
b.notes: Moved: the museum used temporary premises before its new building opened on Plac Defilad (Marszałkowska) in October 2024. Those were offices at ul. Pańska 3 and the Museum over Vistula pavilion for exhibitions. The result says a directory listing still shows Pańska 3, which is out of date, so I gave the newer address. The search summaries did not say which of the listed Links carries the address line, so the three URLs are the Links entries about this museum (city-listing, Wikipedia and Warsaw city office pages). A second search said the building is on the eastern side of Marszałkowska and the first said the western side; this is about the side of the street, not the address. The museum's own site (artmuseum.pl) was not returned by any of the 3 searches, so the address is not confirmed from the museum's own pages.

a.address_statement: Constant's current contact page lists its office at Fortstraat 5A in Saint-Gilles (1060 Brussels). The office is open from Monday to Friday (10h-17h), but it is best to call beforehand.
a.notes: Constant describes itself as an organisation, not a space; the Saint-Gilles office (open Mon-Fri 10h-17h, libraries open to visitors) is the only address presented with public opening hours, so I took it as the main public venue, but this is a judgement call. A second venue exists: a studio at Chaussée de Jette 388 in Koekelberg, visits only by prior email (not chosen). Some older pages show Fortstraat 5, 1060 Brussels, and a 2015 project page gives Rue du Fort 5 (same street, French name; treated as earlier or variant forms, I chose the current contact page's 5A). A Dutch contact page also appeared in the links (https://constantvzw.org/site/Contact,429.html) but the summary did not say which page carried the address, so only the English Contacts page is cited. No report of Constant moving was found. The office is in the Saint-Gilles neighbourhood and shared with le p'tit ciné per the office page (https://constantvzw.org/site/Constant-Office.html), which gives no street number in the summary.

b.notes: No street address found in 3 searches. The only location text, from the Project: About page (https://constantvzw.org/site/Constant-Office.html), says the office is in the neighbourhood of Saint-Gilles, in the south of Brussels, near the Parvis de Saint-Gilles square. The team has worked from that space since 1997 and it is used for administration, meetings and occasional small public events. The office is shared with another association and there is a studio space nearby. The Creating Commons profile says Constant is not a space, it is an organisation. This is not a street, number and postcode. It also does not clearly identify a main public venue, so I left the address empty. One older listing shows an email and phone (info@constantvzw.com, tel and fax ++ 32 2 539 24 67) that may be out of date. The search 'constantvzw.org contact' returned only unrelated pages.

a.address: Pedro de Alba 232, Iztaccihuatl, Benito Juárez, 03520 CDMX
a.address_statement: The CDMX tourism listing describes Biquini Wax EPS as an independent arts project space. It gives the address as Pedro de Alba 232, Iztaccihuatl, Benito Juárez, 03520 CDMX.
a.notes: Name clash: the record's "Bikini Wax EPS" is spelled "Biquini Wax EPS" in the Mexico City government tourism listing, which describes it as an independent arts project space, so I treated it as the same institution; the many Fresha bikini-waxing salon listings in other results are namesakes and were ignored. The record has no website, so there is no own-site confirmation; the only source is this one official city listing. Caveats: the listing is undated (the summary says about 1,337 days old) and a second CDMX map listing places it near the Señor del Buen Despacho Church and San Sebastián Xoco, without a street address. No source reported a move, so there is no newer address, but the address could be stale; verify against the venue's Instagram.

b.address: Pedro de Alba 232, Iztaccihuatl, Benito Juárez, 03520 CDMX
b.address_statement: The Mexico City government's venue directory lists it as Biquini Wax EPS, and gives the address as Pedro de Alba 232, Iztaccihuatl, Benito Juárez, 03520 CDMX.
b.notes: Single source only: the Mexico City tourism venue listing, which spells the name 'Biquini Wax EPS'. The record has no website and no institutional site was found. The result text did not describe what kind of venue it is, so the identity rests on the name match plus 'EPS', the city and the official Mexico City venue directory. The Fresha waxing-salon pages in the results did not name this venue and were ignored. No older or conflicting address appeared. The listing also names a nearby Casa de Cultura Iztaccíhuatl about 0.21 km away. Treat as moderate confidence until a second source confirms.

agreed: Pedro de Alba 232, Iztaccihuatl, Benito Juárez, 03520 CDMX

a.address_statement: The practical-info page lists its permanent location as Coolhaven 32, 3024 AC Rotterdam.
a.notes: Moved: TENT left Witte de Withstraat 50 (3012 BR Rotterdam), where it opened on 9 September 1999, for Coolhaven 32, a former harbour laboratory; the official practical page and the museum.nl listing both give Coolhaven 32. Monoskop said in 2024 it was about to relocate to Coolhaven; the exact move date is not stated in the results (a Uitagenda listing mentions an inauguration on 29 and 30 March, year not stated). Witte de Withstraat 50 still appears on some older pages and is the former address, not chosen. Current event pages also mention a festival-site venue at Schiehaven 17 (an out-of-house programme, not the main venue). Phone numbers differ between pages (+31 10 201 0960 vs 010 4135498), which does not affect the address.

b.address_statement: The museumnacht listing gives the address as Coolhaven 32, 3024 AC Rotterdam, and describes it as a production house for Rotterdam artists with a permanent base on Coolhaven plus nomadic projects.
b.notes: Moved: TENT opened on 9 September 1999 at Witte de Withstraat 50 and relocated to Coolhaven 32. Rotterdam.info says 'TENT has now packed its bags and moved to the new address: Coolhaven 32 after 25 years on Witte de Withstraat'. The new location was inaugurated on 29 and 30 March (year not stated in the result). Older listings still show the former address Witte de Withstraat 50: artstalkmagazine.nl, e-flux and the Wikimedia/osmand category page. I gave the newer address because several independent listings (museumnacht010, museum.nl, uitagendarotterdam, rotterdam.info) agree on Coolhaven 32. Phone numbers and opening hours differ between listings (not part of this field). The official site tentrotterdam.nl was not returned by any search, so this is not confirmed from TENT's own pages.

a.notes: Left empty because the sources disagree and I could not tell which venue is the main one. The official contact page (https://www.catalystarts.org.uk/contact) lists the gallery at 5 College Court, Belfast, BT1 6BS (Tue-Sat 11am-5pm) and 'also gives a second venue at 6 Joys Entry, Belfast'. Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalyst_Arts) gives 5 College Ct, Belfast BT1 6BS. A charity register entry gives 6 Joy's Entry, Belfast, BT1 4DR (the result text did not say which of the listed URLs it was; likely https://opencharities.uk/ni/102342), and a 2026 members' show listing was said to place the gallery at 6 Joys Entry. This points to a possible move from College Court to Joys Entry, but the official page still lists College Court first and calls Joys Entry a second venue, so no move is confirmed. A search for a move found nothing relevant (it returned a different organisation, Catalyst, the science hub). Phone numbers on the sources also differ (028 9013 5061 on the contact page, 02890313303 in an older listing).

b.address_statement: "The organisation's website lists 6 Joys Entry, Belfast, with opening hours of Tuesday – Saturday 11am – 5pm." (result for https://catalystarts.org.uk/about) | "Address: 6 Joy's Entry, Belfast, BT1 4DR." (OpenCharities listing for Catalyst Arts Ltd, charity 102342) | "Its 2023/24 trustee annual report gives its Registered address: 6 Joy's Entry, Belfast."
b.notes: Sources conflict and the address appears to have moved. Older address: 5 College Court, Belfast, BT1 6BS (Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalyst_Arts as '5 College Ct, Belfast BT1 6BS'; In Your Pocket as '2nd Floor, 5 College Court, Belfast'; a third result also gave 'Catalyst Arts 5 College Court Belfast, Northern Ireland, BT1 6BS'). I chose 6 Joy's Entry because the organisation's own site, the charity listing and the 2023/24 annual report agree on it, and the third-party listings with College Court look like older data. Caveats: (1) the WebSearch tool returned synthesised summaries, not raw page text, so the quoted lines come from those summaries; (2) the official site gives 'Joys Entry' with no postcode, and the postcode BT1 4DR comes only from the OpenCharities listing; (3) the annual report line is a registered address, though the site line is tied to opening hours, which suggests the public venue. The claim that College Court is a former location is the search summary's inference, not a dated statement of a move.

a.address: SAFE Building, Jisr el Wati, St. 93, Zone 66 Adlieh, Beirut
a.address_statement: The 2019 relocation notice gives SAFE Building, Jisr el Wati, St. 93, Zone 66 Adlieh, Beirut PO Box 16-7105. (Second search: 'The center's listed address is SAFE Building, Jisr el Wati, St. 93, Zone 66, Adlieh. It moved into its new location in April 2019'.)
a.notes: Newer address chosen over an older one. Older listings give Building 13, Street 97, Jisr el Wati; the centre moved in April 2019, around its 10th anniversary, into two floors of the SAFE building a short walk from the first site. The street and building detail comes from the 2019 relocation notice (the e-flux announcement and the Forum Permanente copy are the same notice; the result text did not say which of the listed URLs carries the line). The official site (https://beirutartcenter.org/about/) states only 'Jisr el Wati, off Corniche an-Nahr, in Adlieh, Beirut', so it agrees on the area but the result text did not show the building or street number. No source gave a postcode (the notice gives PO Box 16-7105). A search for a later move found none, but the sources are mostly dated 2019, so the building detail was not re-confirmed on the official page. Phone and opening hours differ between listings; the official site gave +961 (0) 1 397 268.

b.address: SAFE Building, Jisr el Wati, St. 93, Zone 66 Adlieh, Beirut, Lebanon
b.address_statement: "The 2019 announcement says the center relocated to a SAFE Building on Jisr el Wati, St. 93, Zone 66 Adlieh" | "To mark its 10 years anniversary in 2019, BAC has relocated in a new space, walking distance from its previous location, that is housed inside safe, a storage building." | "Beirut Art Center, SAFE Building, Jisr el Wati, St. 93, Zone 66 Adlieh, Beirut PO Box 16-7105, Lebanon."
b.notes: Newer address: BAC moved in 2019 from its original 2009 venue, a converted factory in the same industrial area (no street address for it appeared in the results), to the SAFE building in Jisr el Wati, Adlieh. No source gave a street number or postcode, so none is given. 'PO Box 16-7105' appeared in a postal-address line and was left out of the venue address because it is a mailing box. Another directory wrote it as 'Jisr el wati, off corniche an-nahr, Building Safe, street 93, zone 66 Adlieh'. Caveats: the sources are dated 2019 and I found no later source, either confirming or contradicting the address; the official page https://beirutartcenter.org/about/ turned up in the results, but the summaries did not show it stating a street address, so I did not cite it for the address. The quoted lines come from WebSearch summaries, not raw page text. One listing placed it in the 'Matn district', which conflicts with 'Beirut' only in naming and does not change the street details.

agreed: SAFE Building, Jisr el Wati, St. 93, Zone 66 Adlieh, Beirut

a.address: Aresco Centre (ground floor), Justinian Street, Kantari, Beirut, Lebanon
a.address_statement: The foundation's visit page places it on the ground floor of the Aresco Centre on Justinian Street in Kantari, Beirut, Lebanon.
a.notes: Newer address chosen. The foundation moved from Gemmayzeh (older pages show the Zoghbi Building; third-party directories show a Gouraud Street office) to Kantari. The search result text said the move was announced in early 2023 and the new premises opened in March 2024, citing a Monocle report (https://monocle.com/culture/beiruts-art-scene-is-undergoing-a-revival-here-are-3-cultural-institutions-you-should-seek-out/). Further coverage: https://artasiapacific.com/news/arab-image-foundation-appoints-new-director-and-opens-new-space-in-beirut. The results gave no street number or postcode, so the address is written the way the source gives it. The statement is the search result's wording about the visit page, not a verbatim line from the page. Opening hours differ between the visit page (Mon-Sat) and the about page (Mon-Fri); I did not use them. The official phone is +961 (1) 355 994.

b.address: Aresco Center, Justinien St., Kantari, Beirut, Lebanon
b.address_statement: "Find us at our new address: Arab Image Foundation Aresco Center, Justinien St. Kantari, Beirut, Lebanon T: +9611355994." (official About page, https://arabimagefoundation.org/about) | "A 2023 report said the foundation left its Gemmayzeh home of 11 years for a two-floor, 800-square-meter space at the Aresco building in Kantari."
b.notes: Newer address chosen: the foundation moved from Gemmayzeh (about 11 years there) to the Aresco Center in Kantari, per the official About page and a 2023 report. Older address seen and not chosen: 'Zoghbi Bldg., 4th floor, 337 Gouraud street, Gemmayze' (https://annalindhfoundation.org/node/4405, a directory listing, out of date). Another older directory listed a different phone number, not relevant to the address. No street number or postcode is given in the sources, so none is given here. The page https://arabimagefoundation.org/about_en.html also appeared in the results; I did not use it, as its content was not shown. The quoted lines come from WebSearch summaries, not raw page text.

a.address: Al Raja' Str. Al Masyoon 1887 Ramallah
a.address_statement: Visit Us Al Raja' Str. Al Masyoon 1887 Ramallah 02 298 7374 info@sakakini.org
a.notes: Written as the official site gives it. The result text quoted this 'Visit Us' block for the centre's own site and mentioned the About page; it did not say whether the line is on the About page or the home page, so both sakakini.org URLs are listed. The source gives no house number, and I could not tell whether '1887' is a postcode or a P.O. box number, so it is kept as written. Other listings write it differently: one gives '4 Al Rajaa Str., Al Masyoon, 00970 Ramallah, Palestine' (the result text did not say which URL; candidates were https://mohit.art/network/khalil-sakakini-cultural-center/, https://circlemena.org/circle-index/organisations/Khalil-Sakakini-Cultural-Centre-Foundation-71e4b and https://www.palestinefilminstitute.org/en/directory/sakakini-cultural-center), and the Visit Palestine page (https://visitpalestine.ps/khalil-sakakini-cultural-center/) gives only the Al-Masyoun neighbourhood. All sources agree on Al Masyoon, Ramallah. A search for a move found none, though the results were undated. Opening hours differ between sources and are not part of this record.

b.address: 4 Al Rajaa Street, Al Masyoun, Ramallah, Palestine
b.address_statement: "The center is at 4 Al Rajaa Street, Al Masyoun, Ramallah, Palestine, according to the Mohit.art network listing."
b.notes: Weak evidence: this is the only source that gave a street address. It is a third-party directory listing (mohit.art), not the institution's own site or an official register. The search for sakakini.org returned only unrelated sites (sak.fi, etc.), and sakakini.org/about pages appeared in results without a stated address, so the official site could not be checked. Corroboration is limited to the neighbourhood: a Visit Palestine listing (https://visitpalestine.ps/khalil-sakakini-cultural-center/) says 'Location: Al-Masyoun neighborhood, Ramallah', which matches but gives no street. An older Art Factories profile (https://artfactories.net/-Palestine-140-.html) gave only a postal address, '1887 Ramallah', which is a PO box and not a venue address, and was not used. No postcode appeared. Treat the street line as unverified against the official site; the quoted line comes from a WebSearch summary, not raw page text.
